habitat: In summer, large flocks feed in grassland, farmland and bushveld, often with Abdim’s Stork. It tends to avoid large permanent floodplains and marshes. Birds are also seen singly or in small groups.
summary: A common summer visitor and resident. A large black-and-white stork with a red bill and red legs. In flight the tail is white, unlike the Yellow-billed Stork. Flocks often soar on hot days and may stay only a few days where food is abundant.

similar.note: Yellow-billed Stork has a yellow bill and a red face. In flight the White Stork is told by its white tail.
Abdim’s Stork is smaller and mostly black, with a white belly and rump.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^12=4096 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 2048–8192.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

wings.pattern: Black and white. The tail is white.

viewNotes.note: Large black-and-white stork with a red bill and red legs, often in a flock.
White tail, which separates it from a Yellow-billed Stork.

calls.description: Newman does not describe the call. The file is a grade A juvenile call from Vains, France, and the filename is Cigogneblanche_juv. The licence is CC0.
